subject.title: fix(secrets): keep standalone-tool provider credentials active when a different provider is selected

question: Should an effectively enabled plugin that declares standalone tools activate its provider SecretRef even when that provider is not selected for generic web search or web fetch?
rationale: Current documentation defines non-selected provider keys as inactive, while this PR deliberately makes a subset active and potentially startup-blocking; that tradeoff is a product security-boundary policy choice, not a purely mechanical correction.

options.title: Confirm the standalone-tool exception
options.body: Treat credentials required by effectively enabled declared standalone tools as active, then document the exception and test valid and unavailable-ref behavior.

options.title: Keep selected-provider-only activation
options.body: Preserve the existing inactive-surface rule and design a separate explicit tool activation or credential-loading contract for standalone tools.

recommendation.title: Confirm the standalone-tool exception
recommendation.body: Treat credentials required by effectively enabled declared standalone tools as active, then document the exception and test valid and unavailable-ref behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available evidence-backed routing candidate because the current active-surface policy is documented in a page they recently contributed to.
